messages.subject: DArT SNP file not read in correctly
parts:
Hi Everyone,
I'm new to DArT-R. So far I've successfully managed to analyze few .csv files with DArT-R package. This time i have a file merged from to different reports. It's coma "," separated file -one row format containing over 86 000 SNPs. The AllelIDs are unique so are the accession names. I have other reports that can be loaded no problem. Any idea what can couse this type of warning?

Regards,
Anna

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] DArT SNP file not read in correctly
parts:
Hi,

just a guess. when you merged the two files there could be snps that have the same alleleid (cloneid is old i need to change the warning), so essentially some snp have the same name. e.g. add a „+1“ to the alleleid of one of the files and check if the warnings goes away.

or sometimes especially excel adds empty rows to the end of files (a bunch of commas) make sure you delete them and try again.

hope that helps,

Bernd

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] DArT SNP file not read in correctly
parts:
Hi Anna,

Welcome to dartR.

DArT when it produces its reports can assign unique identifiers to the sequence tags (CloneID) that carry over from study to study, but it requires a request and considerable additional analysis. Normally they do not do this, so there is a chance that the clone IDs might not be unique when you combine two datasets yourself. This is not a big problem provided you are aware of it. In your first one-row dataset, prepend an A_ to your CloneID values (and/or your AlleleID values) and a B_ for the second one row dataset, then combine manually in excel or an editor and read in.

If your datasets are really large and you do not want to risk having Excel adulterate the data (a good editor will not do this -- notepad++), then you can read each dataset in separately to dartR, use R commands to add the A_ and B_ prefixes in each case, then join the two genlight objects using gl.join() in the latest beta version of dartR. The individual/specimen labels have to be the same in each dataset, and in the same order.

The third option would be to ask DArT to run another service for you combining the relevant plates. They might charge you ($200). This is probably the easiest option if all your samples are on discrete plates and not mixed with other samples you do not want to include in the service. If they are mixed up with other samples, you will need to request a csv file listing the specimens on all plates (and DArT metacolumns), and delete those you do not want to include, then put in the request with the editted specimen listing.

Hope this helps. Let us all know how it goes.

Arthur

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] DArT SNP file not read in correctly
parts:
Hi, 
Thank you for your response.

I've ordered two separate reports from DArT from the same experimental data. One Report includes over 400 accessions and one has only 300. I've noticed that there are unique SNPs discovered for the common pool of accessions in both reports. I've filtered just those SNPs and merged the data frames in R. I want to use DArT-R to recalculate the metrics and filter for MAF and call rate to check if there are any additional SNPs that could be used for genetic distance analysis etc. Please let me know if the problem you mentioned could cause the warning I'm getting or is it just the inconsistency in further analysis?? 

Regards,
Anna
